rationale: Tíw is the Old English name for the Germanic war deity (cognate with Norse Týr and Latin *Deus*), a polytheistic divine figure who controls a specific domain (war/justice), which fits deity.n.01 ("any supernatural being worshipped as controlling some part of the world") far better than the monotheistic god.n.01 or the metaphorical god.n.03. The attestations in glossaries (Wrt. Voc.) confirm it is used as a lexical equivalent for a pagan deity name, not the Christian God.
